A1.justification: The shared FineAction benchmark, annotation examples and matching retrieval results establish continuity despite substantial changes in title, method and scope. Both PDFs are readable, including their equations, tables, figures and complete appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments in Tables 2–5, embedding visualizations and a context-length analysis in Figures 6–8.

after.justification: v2 reports original captioning, retrieval and training-stage ablation results in Tables 2–5, with additional retrieval results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: v1 trains video MLLM embeddings using PromptEOL or AnglE on text-only NLI data. v2 introduces Qwen2-VL-based CARE with video-caption alignment followed by text-only contrastive retrieval adaptation, supporting both caption generation and embeddings. The added alignment stage changes the procedure substantially; the AnglE alternative disappears.

E1.justification: The 1,000-video FIBER benchmark is retained as CAREBENCH, while actual task coverage expands to detailed video captioning. Training additionally uses subsets of Tarsier Recap and LLaVA-Video-178k. MSR-VTT, MSVD and DiDeMo evaluation remains present in Appendix A.

E2.justification: The six CLIP-based retrieval comparators remain, but v2 adds unadapted MLLMs and contrastively trained Tarsier and Qwen2-VL to the retrieval comparisons. Its new captioning comparison includes GPT-4o mini, InternVL2.5 and other MLLMs. The earlier AnglE-trained comparison rows are removed.

E3.justification: v2 introduces DeepSeek-V3-based CapST caption evaluation, replaces the reported S/T bias measure with ReBias, and adds training-stage controls with averaged retrieval, captioning and unified scores. The new alignment stage uses 16-frame training. Ordinary retrieval retains the 32-frame, zero-shot protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds a four-configuration ablation testing alignment and retrieval adaptation separately and jointly. It removes v1’s modality-gap visualization and context-length sensitivity study. The logits analysis is revised from MiniCPM-V’s top 30 English words to Qwen2-VL/CARE’s top 50 tokens; Appendix C largely relocates existing caption-example discussion.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experimental results. The added results continue to use point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive captioning, CARE and ablation results, including CARE general-retrieval R@1 of 77.0/79.0 and overall action/object caption F1 of 35.1/31.7. Matched InternVL2 retrieval entries also change: general-retrieval R@1 moves from 71.6/71.6 to 72.1/73.6. Many CLIP results remain identical, while AnglE and removed-analysis results disappear.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.4 introduces mathematical definitions for ReBias and CapST, including a ratio-deviation measure and NLI-based element matching. v1’s AnglE objective and angle-difference definitions disappear, while its contrastive objective is retained. This substantially revises the mathematical specification, although neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from a retrieval benchmark and VLLE embeddings to a captioning-and-retrieval benchmark, two evaluation metrics and a unified two-stage model. The abstract and conclusion claim capability across both tasks; v1’s conclusions about long effective context and handcrafted embedding modification are dropped.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes relatively small bias for several models, modality-gap removal and possible embedding editing. v2 emphasizes spatial preference, interprets its ablation as evidence that captioning and retrieval training can benefit each other, and explicitly acknowledges that CARE does not resolve spatiotemporal bias.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new alignment recipe, including eight H800 GPUs, 16 frames, a 460,800-pixel limit, batch size 64 and learning rate 2e-5. It specifies captioning prompts and the judge model, and newly discloses two independent annotators per video. The contrastive training settings largely remain, while AnglE/LoRA details disappear and the stated project address changes.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially into detailed captioning, contrasting CAREBENCH with DREAM-1K/AutoDQ and VDC/VDCScore. The paper positions CARE as unifying specialized retrieval and captioning approaches, adds relevant model, dataset and evaluation references, and removes the AnglE reference.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contributions and method narrative are extensively rewritten around CAREBENCH and CARE. Statistics are incorporated into the benchmark section, conventional retrieval experiments move to Appendix A, and the annotation guidelines and caption-example discussion are reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 adds captioning and ablation tables, replaces the introductory retrieval example with a performance bar chart, redraws the training diagram and logits visualization, and expands retrieval-table groupings. The modality-gap plot, context-length plot and word cloud disappear; conventional retrieval tables move to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful captioning evaluations, training-stage controls and an explicit bias limitation, but removes modality-gap and context-length analyses. Important new evidence is inconsistent: Equation (1) implies CLIP B/16 ReBias of about 15.08%, versus 17.75% in Table 4; Table 5’s Qwen2-VL baseline average R@1 is 25.6, versus 31.9 implied by Table 3. The PDFs do not resolve whether these are reporting mistakes or substantive evaluation differences. These gains and reliability concerns prevent a confident net quality judgment.
